# Vendor model libraries

This note describes the third-party SPICE models used by the PSpice for TI project in this folder. It covers the OPAx192 op amp, the TMUX6136 behavioral switch, and the INA828 instrumentation amplifier. Every fact comes from a file read or a simulation run while writing this note. Items that were not verified are listed in section 6.

## 1. Overview

The `vendor/` folder holds model files and symbol libraries that the project does not own. Its contents are listed below.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `vendor/sbom862f/` | TI OPAx192 package: model, symbol library, index, signature, error log, example test project |
| `vendor/tmux6136/` | TMUX6136 behavioral model (`SPDT_PREC`), symbol library, translator log, index, error log |
| `vendor/README.md` | This note |

### Git tracking

The `.gitignore` file ignores the whole folder with two rules. Line 33 reads `vendor/*`, and line 34 reads `!vendor/README.md`. Only this README is tracked. The other files in `vendor/` stay ignored. `git check-ignore` confirms that `vendor/README.md` is not.

### How the project references the libraries

The project file `ti-pspice.opj` registers the model libraries in its "Model Libraries" folder. It lists `vendor\tmux6136\tmux6136_beh.lib` and `vendor\sbom862f\opax192.lib`. It registers the symbol libraries `vendor\sbom862f\OPAx192.OLB` and `vendor\tmux6136\TMUX6136_BEH.OLB`. It also registers `C:\CDS_SPB_HOME\CDSSETUP\PSPTILIBDIR\INA828.OLB` as a symbol library. The project file does not register `INA828.LIB` as a model library.

The generated netlist wrappers (`.cir`) load the models with relative paths. From `lia_sanity.cir`, the lines are:

```
.LIB "../../../vendor/tmux6136/tmux6136_beh.lib"
.LIB "../../../vendor/sbom862f/opax192.lib"
```

The files `frequency_analysis.cir` and `time_analysis.cir` load only `../../../vendor/sbom862f/opax192.lib`. None of the `.cir` files loads the INA828 model by path. All of them load `nom_pspti.lib` through the PSpice netlist settings. That file contains the line `.lib "INA828.LIB"` at line 3825. The library path comes from `LIBPATH` in `PSpice.ini`, which includes `C:\cds_spb_home\cdssetup\pspTILibDir`.

The `.cir` and `.net` files are regenerated by PSpice. The paths above come from the files as they exist now.

The lower-case names in `.opj` and `.cir` do not match the disk names exactly. The disk names are `OPAx192.LIB` and `TMUX6136_BEH.LIB`. Windows matches file names without regard to case, so the references work here. A case-sensitive file system would not find these names.

The header says the model covers the OPA192, OPA2192, and OPA4192 devices. These devices share the same model because they differ only in package.

The signature file `OPAx192.LIBsig` exists. The file `opax192.liberrorLog` contains the text `Signature valid.`

### Pin order

The `.SUBCKT` line at line 88 reads `.SUBCKT OPAx192 IN+ IN- VCC VEE OUT`. The header does not describe the pins. The meanings below follow from the pin names.

| Position | Name | Meaning |

| 1 | IN+ | Non-inverting input |
| 2 | IN- | Inverting input |
| 3 | VCC | Positive supply |
| 4 | VEE | Negative supply |

### Parameters the header claims to cover

The header section "Model Usage Notes" lists these items as modeled:

- Open-loop gain and phase versus frequency, with RL and CL effects (Aol)
- Unity gain bandwidth (GBW)
- Common-mode rejection ratio versus frequency (CMRR)
- Power supply rejection ratio versus frequency (PSRR)
- Differential input impedance (Zid)
- Common-mode input impedance (Zic)
- Open-loop output impedance versus frequency (Zo)
- Output current through the supply (Iout)
- Input voltage noise density versus frequency (en)
- Input current noise density versus frequency (in)
- Output voltage swing versus output current (Vo)
- Short-circuit output current (Isc)
- Quiescent current (Iq)
- Settling time versus capacitive load (ts)
- Slew rate (SR)
- Small-signal overshoot versus capacitive load
- Large-signal response
- Overload recovery time (tor)
- Input bias current (Ib)
- Input offset current (Ios)
- Input offset voltage (Vos)
- Input offset voltage versus temperature (Vos drift)
- Input common-mode voltage range (Vcm)
- Input offset voltage versus input common-mode voltage (Vos vs. Vcm)
- Input and output ESD cells (ESDin, ESDout)

The revision history says the Aol curve was updated "to match the GBW as per the datasheet." It gives no GBW value.

### Key specifications from the header

The header gives no numeric values for the specifications below. Each value is "not stated in the model file."

| Specification | Stated in the model file |
|---|---|
| GBW | Not stated in the model file. The header refers to the datasheet only. |
| Slew rate | Not stated in the model file. Slew rate is listed as modeled. |
| Supply voltage range | Not stated in the model file. |
| Rail-to-rail behavior | Not stated in the model file. Output voltage swing is listed as modeled, but no range is given. |
| Input offset voltage | Not stated in the model file. Offset and offset drift are listed as modeled. |
| Input noise | Not stated in the model file. Voltage and current noise density are listed as modeled. |

The subcircuit body contains parameter values that the header does not explain. The line `X_U4 N25397 N24207 VOS_DRIFT_OPAx192 PARAMS: DC=-2.88E-6 POL=1 DRIFT=0.2E-6` sets an offset block. The line `X_U1 ESDP N24207 VNSE_OPAx192 PARAMS: FLW=0.1 GLF=0.1352 RNV=35.8` sets a noise block. The units and meaning of these values are not stated in the file. They are not verified here, so they should not be read as datasheet values.

### Example test circuit

The folder `vendor/sbom862f/` contains an example project. The project file is `OPAx192_Test_Circuit.OPJ`, and the schematic is `OPAx192_Test_Circuit.DSN`. The schematic file is binary, so its circuit topology and stimulus were not read. The project has two simulation profiles, both listed in `OPAx192_Test_Circuit.OPJ`.

The profile `Aol_Gain` is stored in `OPAx192_Test_Circuit-PSpiceFiles/SCHEMATIC/Aol_Gain.sim`. The profile enables analysis block 1. That block holds the values 81, 100m, and 100MEG. These values describe a frequency sweep from 100 mHz to 100 MHz with 81 points. The sweep type code and the field labels were not verified. The block for the transient analysis is disabled in this profile.

The profile `TRANS` is stored in `OPAx192_Test_Circuit-PSpiceFiles/SCHEMATIC/TRANS.sim`. The profile enables analysis block 0. That block holds the values 2m, 0, and 20u. The name suggests a transient run with a 2 ms time span. The field labels were not verified.

### Error log

The file `opax192.liberrorLog` reports `Signature valid.` It reports no model errors. The signature check covers the library file as delivered by TI.

## 3. TMUX6136_BEH

### What the file models

The file `vendor/tmux6136/TMUX6136_BEH.LIB` contains one behavioral model of a precision single-pole double-throw (SPDT) channel. The subcircuit is named `SPDT_PREC`. The file header describes it as "not a TI model" and as "built from datasheet parameters." The header asks the user to check the values against TMUX6136 datasheet tables 5.5 and 5.6 at plus or minus 15 V. Those tables were not read, so the values were not checked against the datasheet. The header names the file `TMUX6136_BEH_v2.lib`. The file on disk is `TMUX6136_BEH.LIB`. The header says the version is v2, and the changes are convergence fixes.

The file contains one `.SUBCKT`, so there is one subcircuit.

### Pin order

The `.SUBCKT` line reads `.SUBCKT SPDT_PREC S1 S2 D SEL VDD VSS`. The header describes the pins as "S1 S2 D SEL VDD VSS."

| Position | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | S1 | First switch terminal. Connected to D when SEL is low. |
| 2 | S2 | Second switch terminal. Connected to D when SEL is high. |
| 3 | D | Common terminal of the switch |
| 4 | SEL | Logic select input |
| 5 | VDD | Positive supply node. Not modeled, tied to 0 V through 1 GΩ. |
| 6 | VSS | Negative supply node. Not modeled, tied to 0 V through 1 GΩ. |

### Parameters

The `.SUBCKT` line declares these parameters: `RON=120 CS=4p CD=6p QINJ=0.4p TAU=30n ILK=0.5p`. The file gives no units. The units below follow the SPICE convention and the way each parameter is used in the file.

| Parameter | Default | Unit (inferred) | Used in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RON | 120 Ω | ohm | Resistors `R_A` and `R_B`, one in each path from S1 or S2 to D | Series on-resistance of each channel path. It adds to the switch resistance of 0.1 Ω. |
| CS | 4 pF | farad | Capacitors `C_S1` and `C_S2` from S1 and from S2 to 0 V | Parasitic capacitance of each source terminal. |
| CD | 6 pF | farad | Capacitor `C_D` from D to 0 V | Parasitic capacitance of the common terminal. |
| QINJ | 0.4 pC | coulomb | Capacitor `C_INJ` from X to D, value QINJ/1 V = 0.4 pF | Charge injected into D when the internal control edge moves by 1 V. |
| TAU | 30 ns | second | Resistor `R_T` (1 kΩ) and capacitor `C_T` (TAU/1k = 30 pF) | Time constant that slows the internal control edge. |
| ILK | 0.5 pA | ampere | Current source `I_LK` from D to 0 V | DC leakage current drawn from D. |

The parameters RON, CS, CD, QINJ, TAU, and ILK are the only parameters in the file. The file has no parameter named VTH. The file also has no parameters for the switch thresholds or the logic table. Those values are fixed in the file text, as listed below.

### Fixed values in the file

These values are not parameters. They are written directly in the file.

| Element | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `E_LOG` table | Output 0 at SEL of 1.0 V or less, output 1 at SEL of 1.8 V or more, linear between | Converts SEL to an internal control level X0 |
| `R_T` | 1 kΩ | Series resistor with `C_T` |
| `SW_A` | RON = 0.1 Ω, ROFF = 1e10 Ω, VON = 0.3 V, VOFF = 0.4 V | Switch between S1 and NA |
| `SW_B` | RON = 0.1 Ω, ROFF = 1e10 Ω, VON = 0.7 V, VOFF = 0.6 V | Switch between S2 and NB |
| `R_VDD`, `R_VSS` | 1 GΩ to 0 V | Keep the supply nodes from floating |

The file header says the logic threshold is about 1.4 V, which is the midpoint of the 1.0 V and 1.8 V table points.

### Instances in LIA.net

The file `ti-pspice-PSpiceFiles/LIA/LIA.net` creates two instances. Each instance is one SPDT channel. The instance lines are, in full:

```
X_U1 N00890 REF N00695 N00261 VDC 0 SPDT_PREC PARAMS:  RON=120 CS=4P
+  CD=6P QINJ=0.4P TAU=30N ILK=0.5P VTH=1.4
X_U3 N00890 REF N01681 N01577 VDC 0 SPDT_PREC PARAMS:  RON=120 CS=4P
+  CD=6P QINJ=0.4P TAU=30N ILK=0.5P VTH=1.4
```

The pins connect as follows.

| Pin | X_U1 node | What the node is | X_U3 node | What the node is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | N00890 | Input sine: `V_V4` (offset 2.5 V plus `ost`, amplitude `Vampl` = 2 V, frequency `fin`) in series with the harmonic source `V_V7` | N00890 | Same input sine |
| S2 | REF | Reference source `V_V8`, `{Vref}` = 2.5 V | REF | Same reference source |
| D | N00695 | Input IN+ of `X_U2` (OPAx192) | N01681 | Input IN+ of `X_U4` (OPAx192) |
| SEL | N00261 | Pulse `V_V2`: 0 V to 5 V, period 1.934 ms (517 Hz), high for T/2 starting at 0 s | N01577 | Pulse `V_V6`: 0 V to 5 V, period 1.934 ms, starts high after a delay of 482.6 us |
| VDD | VDC | 5 V supply `V_V1` | VDC | 5 V supply `V_V1` |
| VSS | 0 | Ground | 0 | Ground |

The two SEL pulses have the same period. The pulse for X_U1 is high in the first half of each period. The pulse for X_U3 is high in the second half. The two channels therefore have complementary select timing, as read from the netlist.

The netlist overrides every parameter with a value equal to its default. The table below compares them.

| Parameter | Value in LIA.net | Model default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| RON | 120 Ω | 120 Ω | None |
| CS | 4 pF | 4 pF | None |
| CD | 6 pF | 6 pF | None |
| QINJ | 0.4 pC | 0.4 pC | None |
| TAU | 30 ns | 30 ns | None |
| ILK | 0.5 pA | 0.5 pA | None |
| VTH | 1.4 V | Not a parameter of the model | None in the model text as read |

The `VTH` value is passed to the subcircuit but the model text does not use it. The threshold is fixed at 1.0 V and 1.8 V in the table. The symbol library `TMUX6136_BEH.OLB` contains the strings "VTH," "RON," "CS," "CD," "QINJ," "TAU," and "ILK." The symbol therefore carries a VTH property. Its effect on the model was not verified.

### Select input logic

The header says that SEL low connects S1 to D, and that SEL high connects S2 to D. A simulation confirms this rule.

The table `E_LOG` turns SEL into an internal level X0. X0 is 0 V when SEL is at or below 1.0 V. X0 is 1 V when SEL is at or above 1.8 V. The resistor `R_T` and the capacitor `C_T` filter X0 into the node X, with a time constant of 30 ns. Both switches use X as their control voltage, measured against node 0.

Switch `SW_A` connects S1 to NA. Its VON (0.3 V) is less than its VOFF (0.4 V). In PSpice, a switch with VON less than VOFF is on when the control voltage is below VON and off when the control voltage is above VOFF. So `SW_A` closes when X is low, which is when SEL is low.

Switch `SW_B` connects S2 to NB. Its VON (0.7 V) is greater than its VOFF (0.6 V). The usual sense applies. The switch is on when X is above 0.7 V and off when X is below 0.6 V. So `SW_B` closes when X is high, which is when SEL is high.

The model thresholds therefore give this rule. With SEL low, S1 is connected to D. With SEL high, S2 is connected to D. Between X of 0.4 V and 0.6 V, both switches are open. This is the break-before-make window that the header mentions.

#### Simulation evidence

The test circuit `circuits/spdt_prec_select_test.cir` drives S1 with 1 V DC and S2 with 2 V DC. It drives SEL with a 0 V to 5 V pulse. It loads D with 1 MΩ. It was run with this command from the project root:

```
python tools/run_sim.py circuits/spdt_prec_select_test.cir --name vendor_spdt --probe "V(D)" "V(SEL)"
```

The results are in `sim-runs/vendor_spdt/vendor_spdt.csd`. The values of V(D) at the sampled times are these.

| Time | V(SEL) | V(D) | Connected source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 ms | 0 V | 0.9999 V | S1 (1 V) |
| 1.0 ms | 0 V | 0.9999 V | S1 (1 V) |
| 1.5 ms | 5 V | 2.0000 V | S2 (2 V) |
| 2.0 ms | 5 V | 2.0000 V | S2 (2 V) |
| 2.5 ms | 0 V | 0.9999 V | S1 (1 V) |

The transition was also sampled at about 0.01 µs to 0.1 µs spacing around 1.0 ms. V(D) stays near 1.01 V while X crosses the window, then moves to 1.86 V and to 2.0 V within a few tenths of a microsecond. The sampling is too coarse to show a clear open interval. The break-before-make window is therefore taken from the model thresholds, not measured directly. The simulated V(D) also shows a small dip to about 0.99 V and an overshoot to about 2.02 V during the transitions.

#### Consequence for LIA

In the LIA netlist, S1 is the input sine from `V_V4` (2.5 V offset, 2 V amplitude in the netlist default, `fin` = 518 Hz in the GUI default). S2 is the node REF, fed by `V_V8` at 2.5 V. The output D drives the IN+ input of the op amp.

For `X_U1` and the op amp `X_U2`, the IN+ input sees the reference (S2, REF at 2.5 V) during the half period when SEL is high, which is the first half of each 1.934 ms period at 517 Hz. It sees the input sine (S1) during the half period when SEL is low.

For `X_U3` and the op amp `X_U4`, the timing is complementary. The IN+ input sees the input sine (S1) during the first half of each period and the 2.5 V reference (S2) during the second half.

The mapping is the same as the header rule. The intended role of this switching in the LIA demodulator was not checked here. The LIA results were not re-simulated in this note.

### Log files

The file `TMUX6136_BEH.err` is the translator log from the schematic symbol creation on 26 October 2026 at 08:59:43. It reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. It reports that the symbol library `TMUX6136_BEH.olb` was created for the subcircuit `SPDT_PREC`.

The file `tmux6136_beh.liberrorLog` reads `Can't find signature File`. No signature file exists for the TMUX6136 library. This message reports a missing signature file, not a model error.

The file `tmux6136_beh.ind` is a binary index. It was not parsed in this work.

## 4. INA828

### Where the model lives

The INA828 model is not in `vendor/`. The model is `C:\CDS_SPB_HOME\CDSSETUP\PSPTILIBDIR\INA828.LIB`. The same folder holds `INA828.LIBsig`, `INA828.OLB`, and `INA828.OLBlck`. The model is loaded through `nom_pspti.lib` at line 3825, as described in section 1.

The search `grep -ril "SUBCKT INA828"` in `C:\Cadence\PSpiceTI\tools\pspice\library` found no match. The model is not in that folder.

### Model identity

| Item | Value (from `INA828.LIB` header) |
|---|---|
| Subcircuit name | `INA828` |
| Model version | Final 1.4 |
| Model date | 09 DEC 2022 |
| Datasheet cited | SBOS792A (August 2017, revised January 2018) |
| Model type | Generic, suitable for all analysis types |
| Copyright | Texas Instruments Incorporated, 2022 |

The `.SUBCKT` line at line 71 reads `.SUBCKT INA828 IN+ IN- VCC VEE OUT REF RG+ RG-`.

### Pin order

| Position | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | IN+ | Non-inverting input |
| 2 | IN- | Inverting input |
| 3 | VCC | Positive supply |
| 4 | VEE | Negative supply |
| 5 | OUT | Output |
| 6 | REF | Reference node for the output. The model text does not describe it further. |
| 7 | RG+ | First terminal of the external gain resistor |
| 8 | RG- | Second terminal of the external gain resistor |

### Header parameters and specifications

The header lists modeled parameters from the same families as the OPAx192 header. These include Aol, GBW, CMRR, PSRR, Zid, Zic, Zo, Iout, en, in, Vo, Isc, Iq, ts, slew rate, overshoot, large-signal response, tor, Ib, Ios, Vos, Vos drift, Vcm, Vos versus Vcm, and ESD cells. The header lines read (lines 1 to 70) contain no numeric specification values. Gain, bandwidth, noise, and offset values are therefore "not stated in the model file."

### Gain formula and measured gain

The model file does not state the gain formula. The datasheet formula is G = 1 + 50 kΩ / RG (datasheet SBOS792). The datasheet was not read in this work, so the formula is taken from the project review, not from a file read here.

The test circuit `circuits/ina828_gain_test.cir` checks the formula. It applies a 1 V AC differential input (IN+ at 1 V AC, IN- at 0 V), sets RG to 5 kΩ, ties REF to 0 V, and uses +5 V and -5 V supplies. It runs an AC sweep from 10 Hz to 10 kHz. It was run with this command from the project root:

```
python tools/run_sim.py circuits/ina828_gain_test.cir --name ina828_gain --probe "V(OUT)" "V(IN+)"
```

The measured gain at 1 kHz is 11.00 V/V (20.83 dB), with V(OUT) = 11.0000 V and V(IN+) = 1.0000 V. The formula gives 11 V/V for RG = 5 kΩ, so the measured value matches. The gain was also 11.00 V/V at 10 Hz and 100 Hz, and it rose to 11.002 V/V at 10 kHz. The test checks one value of RG only.

### Instance in differential-amplifier.net

The file `ti-pspice-PSpiceFiles/differential-amplifier/differential-amplifier.net` contains this instance:

```
X_U1 N09301 N09296 +5V -5V VDIFF 0 N07217 N07227 INA828
```

| Pin | Node | What the node is |
|---|---|---|
| IN+ | N09301 | Positive input. Connected to `V_V6` (DC 0 V, AC 1 V). |
| IN- | N09296 | Negative input. Connected to `V_V6`. |
| VCC | +5V | Positive supply, derived from `V_V4` (5 V) through `R_R14` (3 Ω) |
| VEE | -5V | Negative supply, derived from `V_V5` (5 V below ground) through `R_R15` (3 Ω) |
| OUT | VDIFF | Output. Feeds the filter chain through `C_C1`. |
| REF | 0 | Ground |
| RG+ | N07217 | Gain resistor node. Connected to `R_R16`. |
| RG- | N07227 | Gain resistor node. Connected to `R_R16`. |

The resistor `R_R16` connects RG- and RG+ and has a value of 5 kΩ. With the formula above, the stage gain for this netlist is 11 V/V.

The generated file `differential-amplifier.net` does not name the library. The library is resolved through `nom_pspti.lib`, as described in section 1.

## 5. Usage notes for agents

The table below lists each model. The pin order is the order of the `.SUBCKT` line. A netlist instance must list its nodes in the same order.

| Model | Subckt name | Pin order | Library file | Used in designs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OPAx192 (TI, Final 1.7) | `OPAx192` | IN+ IN- VCC VEE OUT | `vendor/sbom862f/OPAx192.LIB` | LIA (`X_U2`, `X_U4`), differential-amplifier (`X_U2`, `X_U3`) |
| TMUX6136 behavioral SPDT (not TI, v2) | `SPDT_PREC` | S1 S2 D SEL VDD VSS | `vendor/tmux6136/TMUX6136_BEH.LIB` | LIA (`X_U1`, `X_U3`) |
| INA828 (TI, Final 1.4) | `INA828` | IN+ IN- VCC VEE OUT REF RG+ RG- | `C:\CDS_SPB_HOME\CDSSETUP\PSPTILIBDIR\INA828.LIB` (loaded by `nom_pspti.lib`) | differential-amplifier (`X_U1`) |

Several points need attention before an agent changes these designs or writes a new circuit file.

The `SPDT_PREC` select rule works as the header says. S1 is connected when SEL is low and S2 when SEL is high. The LIA design depends on this rule. The VTH parameter in `LIA.net` has no effect in the model text.

Use `.LIB` or `.INC` correctly when writing a `.cir` by hand. The rule depends on whether the library is signed.

- The home-made `SPDT_PREC` library (`vendor/tmux6136/TMUX6136_BEH.LIB`) has no `.LIBsig` file. In a batch run, `SPDT_PREC` was reported as undefined through `.LIB`. Load this file with `.INC`.
- The TI signed libraries (`OPAx192.LIB` with `OPAx192.LIBsig`, and `INA828.LIB` loaded through `nom_pspti.lib`) must stay `.LIB`. Loaded through `.INC`, the OPAx192 model fails with `ERROR(ORPSIM-16583): More than one imported model containing transistors or diodes`.

`tools/run_sim.py` applies this rule. It rewrites a `.LIB` line to `.INC` only when the target file has no `.LIBsig` file and no `.LIB` sections. It also adds `.OPTIONS FILEMODELSEARCH`. Hand-written circuits that bypass the tool must follow the same rule.

`tools/run_sim.py` converts a probe such as `V(NODE)` to `V([NODE])`, which PSpice needs for node voltages. It runs one PSpice at a time, because `pspice.exe` is single-instance. Run simulations one after another from the project root.

The `.cir` and `.net` files are generated and git-ignored. Edit the schematic in OrCAD Capture instead of editing the generated files.

The test circuits in `circuits/` are small checks for this note. They are not part of any design.

## 6. Items not verified

The following items were not verified in this work. Each one needs a simulation, a datasheet, or the file itself before it is treated as fact.

- The break-before-make window of `SPDT_PREC` between X of 0.4 V and 0.6 V. The transition was sampled, but the open interval was not resolved.
- The LIA results. The SPDT select behavior was checked alone, not inside the full LIA circuit.
- The TMUX6136 values against the TMUX6136 datasheet tables.
- The INA828 gain at RG values other than 5 kΩ. The datasheet formula was not read in this work.
- The function of the INA828 REF pin beyond its name.
- The circuit topology and stimulus of the OPAx192 example project (the `.DSN` file is binary).
- The field labels and sweep type codes in the `.sim` files.
- The contents of the binary index files (`opax192.ind`, `tmux6136_beh.ind`).
- The units of the parameter values inside the OPAx192 and INA828 subcircuit bodies.
- The symbol pin names of `OPAx192.OLB` and `INA828.OLB`. The strings were extracted, but the mapping to pin numbers was not checked.
